statement: KV cache capacity exhibits a sharp binary threshold below which preemptions spike TTFT p99 by 100-250x; above the threshold, TTFT is determined entirely by compute (prefill latency).
regime: BLIS simulation with qwen/qwen3-14b on H100, tp=2, num_instances=2, rate=100 req/s, prefix_tokens=512. Threshold ~4500-5000 blocks at this config.
mechanism: When total_kv_blocks < threshold, the KV cache fills completely and the scheduler must preempt (evict) running requests to make room for new prefills. Preempted requests rejoin the queue and re-prefill from scratch, causing their TTFT to include both the preemption delay and a second prefill. Above the threshold all concurrent requests fit simultaneously, preemption_count = 0, and TTFT reduces to the single-pass prefill latency (~39ms).
applicability_bounds: Threshold scales with GPU count and request rate. Higher throughput tiers (more instances or higher TP) need proportionally more cache blocks to avoid preemption. The binary nature of the threshold (zero preemptions above vs many below) is a general property of FCFS scheduling with cache eviction. Block size (16 vs 32 tokens/block) shifts the threshold slightly.

statement: GPU count (tp * num_instances) is the dominant throughput factor in BLIS, creating discrete throughput tiers; within each tier, KV blocks and max_num_running_reqs have threshold-gated effects while scheduler and block_size are negligible.
regime: BLIS simulation with qwen/qwen3-14b on H100, rate=100 req/s, prefix_tokens=512. Observed across all 200-eval search runs.
mechanism: GPU count determines compute capacity (FLOP/s and memory bandwidth scale with TP and instance count). KV blocks and max_running_reqs each have a threshold below which resource starvation dominates TTFT, but above which they have zero marginal effect. Scheduler (fcfs vs sjf) and block_size (16 vs 32) change only scheduling order and block granularity respectively — neither affects throughput at the cluster level when resources are sufficient.
applicability_bounds: Dominant factor relationship may shift at much lower rates (where a single GPU is sufficient) or at extreme rates where scheduling policy affects batching efficiency. The observation is at rate=100 req/s with 200-request workloads; generalization to higher rates requires verification.

statement: A two-phase adaptive search (structured sampling + neighbor expansion) finds a near-complete Pareto front for the BLIS 6-knob space within 11% of the total configuration budget (200 of 1800 configs), covering all GPU tiers, in under 20 seconds wall time.
regime: BLIS qwen/qwen3-14b on H100, rate=100 req/s, 4-objective Pareto optimization over {tp, num_instances, scheduler, max_running_reqs, total_kv_blocks, block_size}.
mechanism: The search exploits low effective dimensionality: GPU count creates 8 discrete tiers, and within each tier only 2 knobs (KV blocks, max_running_reqs) materially affect Pareto membership. The structured Phase 1 sampling (40% budget) covers all tiers with representative configs. Phase 2 neighbor expansion (60% budget) fills gaps around the Pareto front by exploiting locality — neighbors of Pareto-optimal configs are likely to be Pareto-competitive. The algorithm found 62-80 non-dominated configs across three seeds.
applicability_bounds: Efficiency depends on the space having hierarchical structure with discrete tiers. At different rates or models, the tier boundaries and threshold values may shift, but the search algorithm is rate-agnostic. Generalization to larger search spaces (more knobs or wider value ranges) requires validation.
